newsitem.title: FRANCE: Exiled Algerian calls for overhaul of the FIS.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Algerian calls for overhaul of the FIS.

text.p: An exiled leader of Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) has said an accord with other opposition groups to seek talks with the government was no longer valid and FIS must now seek discussions by itself.

Kamerddine Kherbane also said in an interview to the French weekly L'Evenement du Jeudi released on Wednesday that the FIS political structures had become obsolete as the violence in Algeria worsened.
"We must overhaul our organisation and put new structures into place," Kherbane, a former air force pilot and a founder of FIS, said.
"Thus, the Rome accord (of 1995) is outdated and must no longer be referred to. We must now talk with Algeria's rulers on our own, without any intermediary," he said.
He repeated a FIS demand that its two top leaders, Abassi Madani and Ali Benhaj, be released from their Algerian prison as only they could represent the movement in talks.
"Their release is a condition to any discussion. Otherwise the war will go on," he said.
More than 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria since Moslem fundamentalist rebels took up arms following the cancellation of 1992 elections that FIS was poised to win.
President Liamine Zeroual had proposed parliamentary elections in May or June but said the outlawed FIS would not be allowed to run.
Kherbane said the FIS armed wing, the Islamic Salvation Army (AIS), had nothing to do with worsening massacres of civilians in Algeria or bomb attacks in France.

He said the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), the most ruthless of Algerian rebel groups, which has been blamed for the violence was made up of hardline agents of the Algerian secret servces and Islamists they manipulated.
